01_nested_dyadic_refinement.png.alt: Residues branch from modulus two to four to eight. Each child keeps its parent address modulo the coarser modulus.

02_crt_dyadic_odd_grid.png.alt: A three-by-eight table gives every residue modulo 24 from its residue modulo three and residue modulo eight.

03_refinement_incidence.png.alt: A four-by-twelve incidence matrix assigns each fine residue modulo twelve to its parent modulo four.

04_weighted_transfer_graph.png.alt: Three packets form a directed cycle with weights one, two and one, and loops with weights two, three and four.

05_path_zeta_coefficients.png.alt: Counts of all walks from packet zero to packet two through total weight thirty-six grow on a logarithmic vertical scale above one.

06_filtered_inverse_depth.png.alt: For precisions one through twelve, the largest allowed integer transfer weight is precision minus one.

07_dyadic_delayed_separation.png.alt: Two complementary projectors have rows [one, one half; zero, zero] and [zero, minus one half; zero, one].

08_odd_prime_separation.png.alt: At coefficient primes two, three, five, seven and eleven, the denominator weights are one, zero, zero, zero and zero.

09_refinement_defect_bound.png.alt: Over operator powers one through twelve, the measured defect decreases while its telescoping upper bound increases on a logarithmic norm scale.

10_transfer_block_sparsity.png.alt: A six-by-six table of block norms has nonzero entries only on the diagonal and the two neighboring residue phases.

11_smith_polyphase_orbit.png.alt: Four reflection-coordinate plots retain samples of radius zero point seven two at orders two, four, eight and sixteen.

12_smith_adaptive_weight.png.alt: The logarithm of a symmetric refinement weight increases toward the two boundary points minus one and one of the reflection disk.

13_theorem_dependency.png.alt: Eight separate left-to-right routes connect their own inputs to coordinate, Fourier, CRT, inverse, graph, separation, Smith and defect conclusions.
